issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

An in-place foreach op whose other operand is computed from the same tensor at other positions gives wrong values under `torch.compile`. Eager is fine, and so is the plain `x.add_(x.flip(0))`.

```python
import torch


def f(x):
    torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)])
    return x


device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
compiled = torch.compile(f)
for shape in ((8, 8), (1024, 1024)):
    x = torch.rand(*shape, device=device)
    want = f(x.clone())
    print(shape, [int((compiled(x.clone()) != want).sum()) for _ in range(5)])
```

CUDA, 2.14.0+cu130, RTX 4070 (2.9.1 is the same): right at the small shape, wrong at the large one.

```
(8, 8) [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
(1024, 1024) [496640, 495296, 496560, 495504, 496512]
```

CPU, 2.14.0 and nightly 2.15.0.dev20260921: wrong at any size.

```
(8, 8) [32, 32, 32, 32, 32]
(1024, 1024) [524204, 524184, 524192, 524136, 524244]
```

The kernel gets `x` as input and as output, and reads the mirrored row while it is being written:

```python
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + (x2), xmask)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + (56 + x0 + ((-8)*x1)), xmask)
    tmp2 = tmp0 + tmp1
    tl.store(out_ptr0 + (x2), tmp2, xmask)

triton_poi_fused_0.run(arg0_1, arg0_1, 64, stream=raw_stream0)
```

Same with `x.roll(1, 0)`, `x.T.clone()` or `x.flip(0) * 2.0` as the other operand, with `_foreach_mul_`, `_foreach_copy_` and `_foreach_addcdiv_`, and with lists of more than one tensor.

`register_foreach_inplace` in `torch/_inductor/lowering.py` lowers the op as the out-of-place one followed by `mutate_to(arg, result, unsafe_alias=True)`. With `unsafe_alias`, `realize_into` skips the copy and gives the pointwise that computes `result` the layout `MutationLayoutSHOULDREMOVE(arg)`, which is only safe when `result` reads `arg` at the position it writes. Would checking the read indices there, and falling back to `unsafe_alias=False` otherwise, be the right fix? I can send it.

issue.title: [inductor] torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)]) reads x while writing it: silent wrong results (CUDA and CPU)

issue.body:
Fixes #198033

`register_foreach_inplace` lowers `_foreach_add_(xs, ys)` as the out-of-place op followed by `mutate_to(x, result, unsafe_alias=True)`. With `unsafe_alias`, `realize_into` gives the pointwise that computes `result` the layout `MutationLayoutSHOULDREMOVE(x)`, which is only safe when `result` reads `x` at the element it writes. `torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)])` reads the mirrored row in the kernel that writes it: wrong at every size on CPU, a race on CUDA that shows at 1024 x 1024.

This checks the reads of the pointwise against its write before aliasing. When a read of the target is at another index, the result is realized into a buffer of its own and copied, the way `x.add_(x.flip(0))` is already lowered. An optimizer step reads each parameter where it writes it, so it still writes in place with no extra buffer.

Test plan: `test_inplace_reads_self_elsewhere` in test_foreach.py, which fails without the change. On 2.14 with CUDA (RTX 4070), test_foreach.py is 600 passed, and test_compiled_optimizers.py is 804 passed with and without the change, with the same one pre-existing failure (`test_S429861`).

issue.title: [inductor] Don't write an in-place foreach op straight into a buffer it reads elsewhere

issue.body:
Fixes #198533
Fixes #198033

`mutate_to`'s fast path replaces the data of the mutated StorageBox with the new value. A realized StorageBox may already be referenced by name: by a ReinterpretView, whose loader looks the name up only when it runs, or by an extern kernel's inputs. Everything lowered before the mutation through those references then reads the new value, including the new value itself. With `y = x + x.sum(-2, keepdim=True)` and a mask of `y.roll(-1, -2) == y.transpose(-1, -2)`, `y.index_put_((mask,), v)` gives wrong values on CPU and CUDA. When an mm reads `y.t()` before the fill, the scheduler fails with a `KeyError`.

The fast path is now taken only for a StorageBox that is not realized. A realized one goes through the existing `realize_into` path, which writes the value into its buffer in place. Inputs, module buffers and NopKernels are all realized nodes, so their three checks are gone. Writing in place means two tensors must not share a buffer:

- The `copy_` and `fsdp.copy_` lowerings pass `share_value=False` to `mutate_to`, so the target gets a copy of the source instead of its buffer: if it took the buffer, a later in-place write to either would change both. `propagate_mutation` calls `mutate_to` with `share_value=True` directly instead of going through the `copy_` lowering: what it writes back (after an in-place collective, a mutable custom op or a user Triton kernel whose argument was copied to meet a layout constraint) is that copy, which nothing else reads, so an argument that is not realized can take its buffer as before. A realized argument now gets the copy written into it in place.
- An empty buffer that nothing has written yet keeps the fast path, the value copied into its layout, so `empty_like(x).fill_(0)` generates the same code as before.
- `realize_into` computes an `unsafe_alias` value (the in-place foreach ops) straight into the target only when the value reads the target at the position it writes, as an optimizer step does; otherwise the value gets its own buffer and is copied. This is the check of #198242 and applies to inputs too, so it also fixes #198033 (`torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)])`).

Writing in place also exposes a ConcatKernel bug, found and fixed in #198715: ConcatKernel computes a flexible-layout input straight into the concat buffer, so an in-place mutation of that input after the cat changes the concat. `index_put_` with integer indices after `cat` was already wrong; the masked form was right only because `mutate_to` swung the pointer. The fix is #198715's: GraphLowering collects the fake storages that some node writes in place (including inside control_deps subgraphs), and ConcatKernel copies such inputs instead of computing them into its buffer. The check is conservative on purpose: it looks at the inputs of the node being lowered, and a mutation anywhere in the graph counts. `test_cat_input_mutated_after_cat` and the two control_deps tests are from #198715 too.

Test plan, on 2.14 with the change applied at runtime, on CPU and on CUDA (RTX 4070):

- New tests in test_torchinductor.py: `test_index_put_as_masked_fill_mask_reads_target_view` (wrong values), `..._by_extern_kernel` (`KeyError`), `test_mutate_realized_buffer_in_make_fx_graph` (make_fx graphs that keep `copy_`, `fsdp.copy_`, `add_` and foreach ops, parametrized over five cases), `test_mutable_op_layout_copy_written_back_in_place` (a mutable custom op tagged `needs_contiguous_strides` gets a contiguous copy of a transposed intermediate that an mm has already read through a view; the copy is written back through `propagate_mutation`, and used to replace the intermediate's buffer), `test_cat_input_mutated_after_cat` (parametrized) and `test_masked_fill_of_realized_buffer_kernel_count`, which checks that a masked fill of an mm output stays one kernel written in place (Halide skips it: it won't fuse a read of the buffer a kernel writes in place). All 36 pass in test_torchinductor{,_dynamic_shapes,_codegen_dynamic_shapes}.py on CPU and on CUDA; without the change 20 of them fail on each. The ones that pass without it guard what writing in place could break: the `fsdp.copy_` case fails when only `copy_` copies, and the foreach case on an mm output fails without the check in `realize_into`. test_control_deps.py: 13 passed (the two new tests fail without the change).
- `test_inductor_steal_buffer` and `test_triton_kernel_clone_wekdeps` generate the same code as before. Across the collective, auto_functionalize, user Triton kernel and torchinductor tests below, `propagate_mutation` writes back 18 times, 16 of them into an argument that is not realized, which keeps taking the copy's buffer.
- A/B, same outcome test by test apart from the new tests: on CUDA (2,016 tests) the mutation/copy/fill/index_put/cat/concat/scatter/inplace/foreach/alias selections of the three files, test_inplacing_pass.py, test_auto_functionalize.py, test_control_deps.py, test_distributed_patterns.py (its `fsdp.copy_` graphs write a module parameter, a graph input), test_pattern_matcher.py's `fsdp.copy_` test, test_foreach.py, test_triton_kernels.py KernelTests, TestCollectivesInductor (single rank) and the cat/stack/index_put/scatter/copy OpInfo tests; on CPU (1,385 tests) the same files that run there. test_compiled_optimizers.py on CUDA: 805 passed and 3 skipped either way; the check in `realize_into` runs once per in-place foreach output, 150 times in the compile of a foreach Adam step with 50 parameters on CPU, 0.04 s in total.

Kernels and allocations, before -> after (64x64, the same on CUDA and on the C++ CPU backend; the mm is an extern kernel and is not counted):

| Pattern | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `s = x @ w; s.index_put_((m,), -inf)`, and `s[s < 0] = 0` | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| `fill_`, `add_` or foreach `add_` on an mm output, `empty_like(x).fill_(0)` | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| `copy_` of an mm output into an empty or unrealized buffer | 0 kernels | 1 kernel |
| `copy_` of an mm output into another mm output | 0 kernels, 1 allocation | 1 kernel, 2 allocations |
| foreach `add_` of `y.flip(0)` into an mm output `y` | 1 kernel, 2 allocations | 2 kernels, 2 allocations |
| foreach `add_` of `x.flip(0)` into an input `x` (#198033) | 1 kernel, wrong | 2 kernels, 1 allocation |
| foreach `add_` of another tensor into an input | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| A masked fill of `y` whose mask reads `y.roll(-1, -2)` | 2 kernels | 2 kernels |

The `copy_` and foreach rows on an mm output come only from graphs that keep their mutations (make_fx + compile_fx_inner): torch.compile functionalizes them away.
